## Appearance

Matthew Cuthbert is an odd-looking, ungainly man with stooping shoulders and long iron-gray hair that reaches them. He possesses kindly brown eyes and has worn a full, soft brown beard continuously since the age of twenty.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER II. Matthew Cuthbert Is Surprised P3](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0003), [v1 CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out P34](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0034)_

## Personality

Extremely shy and reticent, Matthew Cuthbert is a quiet, hardworking man who dreads interacting with strangers, women, and little girls. Despite his uncommunicative nature, he is a patient, wise, and good-natured person who serves as a sympathetic listener. While argument is not his strong point, he possesses a remarkable silent persistency and holds fast to his opinions once his mind is set. His quiet nature and preference for a peaceful life mean he never seeks out excitement. Driven by a desire to keep [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), his deep affection and gentle demeanor remain constant, even as others consider him unimportant.

## History

Matthew Cuthbert lived at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) with his sister, [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md). After deciding to adopt an orphan boy from [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia), Matthew traveled to the [Bright River](../codex/places.md#bright-river) station, only to find that a young girl named [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) had arrived by mistake instead. Charmed by her lively talk, he brought her home, where he quietly urged [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) to keep the child despite their original intention. Matthew continued to subtly advocate for [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) as she settled into their lives. Recognizing that her discipline was isolated, he secretly visited her room after an outburst to gently persuade her to apologize to Mrs. [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) so she could re-join the household. 

Matthew frequently provided [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) with quiet encouragement and small comforts, such as treating her to sweets and backing her participation in a local Christmas concert. Noticing that she dressed far more plainly than her peers, he flusteredly navigated a shop encounter and enlisted Mrs. Lynde's help to buy and sew a modern dress with puffed sleeves for Anne's Christmas gift. As [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) grew older, Matthew's pride in her academic success deepened, though his health began to decline over the years.

After [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) tied for first place on the island's entrance exams and eventually earned the Avery scholarship at Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#academy), she returned to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), where Matthew shared a quiet, peaceful walk with her. The next day, after reading news of the Abbey Bank's collapse—where their life savings were held—Matthew collapsed from sudden heart failure and died instantly.

## Quotes

> "Well, she didn’t. She brought her. I asked the stationmaster. And I had to bring her home. She couldn’t be left there, no matter where the mistake had come in."
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P5](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0005)

> “Well now, you’ll have to punish her,” said Matthew, reaching for his hat. “I’ve nothing to do with it, remember. You warned me off yourself.”
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XIV. Anne’s Confession P25](../source/v01-c14.md#nw-v01-c14-p0025)

> “Well now, I’m much obliged,” said Matthew, “and—and—I dunno—but I’d like—I think they make the sleeves different nowadays to what they used to be. If it wouldn’t be asking too much I—I’d like them made in the new way.”
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XXV. Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves P26](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0026)

> "Just mind you that—rather than a dozen boys. Well now, I guess it wasn’t a boy that took the Avery scholarship, was it? It was a girl—my girl—my girl that I’m proud of."
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream P41](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0041)

> "I reckon she ought to be punished a little. But don’t be too hard on her, Marilla. Recollect she hasn’t ever had anyone to teach her right. You’re—you’re going to give her something to eat, aren’t you?"
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P3](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0003)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--matthew-cuthbert.md)

Matthew serves as a gentle, quiet advocate for [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) from the moment he brings her to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables). Unlike [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md), Matthew immediately wants to keep [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) despite the initial mix-up regarding her adoption, quietly supporting her presence in the home. He offers her comfort and sweet treats, even sneaking up to her room to kindly persuade her to apologize to Mrs. [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) so she can be freed from her punishment. Through his quiet affection and indulgence, Matthew helps [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) adjust to her new life and grow up successfully.

- Friend of — good friend who helps her grow up successfully  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXII. Anne Is Invited Out to Tea P10](../source/v01-c22.md#nw-v01-c22-p0010), [v1 CHAPTER XXIV. Miss Stacy and Her Pupils Get Up a Concert P17](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0017), [v1 CHAPTER XXXI. Where the Brook and River Meet P8](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0008)</sub>
